=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review (SPA-N-001 to SPA-N-016)

**Overall:** The draft is weighted heavily toward the Seller. Several known exposures are pushed into the general warranty regime, where caps, baskets and disclosure would limit recovery. The Seller labels the positions "FINAL" and "settled at principal level," but I have no record of any such agreement. Wattlebridge should confirm this internally before conceding anything. The market statements are unsupported assertions, not evidence. Enforceability of the limitation, non-reliance and buyer-knowledge provisions under NSW law should be confirmed by NSW counsel.

**Known exposures:** Riverlark ~AUD 3.2m, bonuses AUD 420k, Ironquay AUD 180k open, Sandbar AUD 330k. Together these total ~AUD 4.13m, which nearly exhausts the Seller's proposed AUD 4.8m general cap before any Bluefen revenue risk (~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue). Known issues should be handled through price, funds flow and specific indemnities, not through warranty claims.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** General warranty liability capped at 20% of price (AUD 4.8m).
- **Buyer wants:** Open at 100% of price. Fallback is a materially higher cap (e.g., 30–50%), with known issues carved out to specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** The cap leaves almost no headroom above the disclosed exposures already identified.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25k per claim; AUD 250k deductible basket (~1.04% of price). Only the excess above the basket is recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis ~AUD 10k, with related claims aggregated. Tipping basket of ~0.5% (AUD 120k), so that once it is exceeded, recovery runs from the first dollar.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** A deductible AUD 250k basket means the buyer absorbs the first quarter-million of any warranty loss.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months from Completion. Limitation applies to all claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24–36 months for general warranties. Tax claims run until 60 days after the ATO amendment period expires. Fundamental claims are carved out (see N-004). Any "applies unless stated" rule should be replaced by express carve-outs.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** 18 months may cover only one audit cycle, and the default-to-all wording would catch categories that need longer periods.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, solvency) outside the general cap, up to 100% of price. Time limit of at least 6 years. Not subject to de minimis or basket.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Buying 100% of the shares means title is the core protection, and it should not sit under a 4.8m cap and 18-month limit.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** No express fraud carve-out. The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** Express carve-out for fraud (including fraud by Seller's officers, employees or agents) from cap, basket, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. Confirm enforceability of the wording with NSW counsel.
- **Recommendation: Add.** As drafted, the limitations would apply to fraud, which is not acceptable.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026), the accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1, 1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete general disclosure. Only specific, fair disclosure against specific warranties, with no deemed disclosure of data-room content. The non-admission wording in DL 1.4 is acceptable.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** General data-room disclosure would negate most of the warranty package.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete. If any version is retained, limit it to actual knowledge of named individuals, excluding "discoverable" matters. Australian authority on pro- and anti-sandbagging is not settled, so this is a drafting point for NSW counsel to confirm.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Known issues belong in specific indemnities and price adjustments. "Discoverable" is an unworkable standard.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours only. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The disclosure letter confirms that no final consent has been provided and clause 11.3 conditions are unsatisfied.
- **Buyer wants:** Unconditional written consent in agreed form, with clause 11.3 conditions satisfied, as a condition precedent to Completion. Buyer-only waiver right. Termination right if not obtained. Specific indemnity or price adjustment for loss of Bluefen revenue if the contract is terminated or varied within an agreed period.
- **Recommendation: Reject the deemer; make it a condition precedent.** Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m).

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** Release of security to be provided after Completion. Facility ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; not repaid; no discharge included.
- **Buyer wants:** On a debt-free basis, the facility is repaid at Completion from the price under a payoff letter in the funds flow. Discharge of security (including PPSR discharge) delivered at Completion. Any change-control consent (cl 8.1) obtained beforehand.
- **Recommendation: Reject the post-Completion release.** It conflicts with the debt-free/cash-free baseline and leaves the Company's assets encumbered after the buyer has paid.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** Bonuses (AUD 420k) are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow. Payroll tax, super and on-costs are not addressed.
- **Buyer wants:** Treat bonuses and all employer on-costs (super, payroll tax, any other statutory costs) as debt-like items deducted from price or paid by the Seller before Completion. Confirm which conditions are triggered by Completion.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** The bonuses are unpriced in the funds flow, and on-costs are unquantified.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment. Described as "adequate."
- **Buyer wants:** Seller to pay all outstanding Ironquay fees before Completion (treated as debt-like). Confirmatory assignment of SOW3 Project Materials as a condition precedent (DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer conditional on payment). Bank evidence of payment status (DD-010's AUD 180k open figure is not bank-verified). Specific indemnity covering any Ironquay IP title or third-party claim, not just the payment, with separate cap and longer survival.
- **Recommendation: Reject as adequate.** A payment-only indemnity does not protect IP title or third-party claims.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- **Seller:** Described as preliminary and "not expected to be material." Not characterised as a breach. No loss amount. Possible export of ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific indemnity for all losses from the DD-006 incident, regardless of how it is characterised. Covers forensic investigation, notification, regulatory response, remediation and third-party claims. Sits outside cap and basket. Seller funds a forensic review before Completion. Privacy counsel to assess Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) notifiable data breach obligations; the Company will carry any obligation after Completion. Consider a retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation: Specific indemnity plus escrow.** Access is unknown, and the regulatory obligations would sit with the Company after Completion.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330k are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Buyer wants:** Review the contracts for term, termination rights, prepayments and whether the three renewals form one commitment (the disclosure describes them as related). Allocate costs by period, so the Seller bears pre-Completion periods. Treat prepayments or out-of-ordinary-course commitments as debt-like.
- **Recommendation: Verify before accepting.** Related renewals may be a single commitment that the "ordinary course" label obscures.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** Collapses all warranties into one regime for "administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** Separate categories, each with its own cap, basket and time limit: (1) fundamental (title, capacity), (2) tax, (3) IP, (4) specific indemnities, (5) general warranties. Fundamental and tax claims excluded from the basket.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** Collapsing categories puts high-risk items under the lowest level of protection.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012, showing Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100%.
- **Buyer wants:** A register entry alone is not verification. Obtain a current ASIC extract, the register of members, share certificates, the chain of prior transfers and board approvals, a PPSR search over the shares, and confirmation that no options or convertibles exist. The disclosure letter confirms the buyer has not yet completed its own verification.
- **Recommendation: Verify.** The title warranty is only as good as the underlying record.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** A pre-Completion tax indemnity covering the Company's pre-Completion tax liabilities, outside basket and general cap. A separate tax warranty set, with time limits running until 60 days after the ATO amendment period expires. A separate IP warranty set (ownership, non-infringement, open source, contractor and employee assignments), linked to the Ironquay position in N-011.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** These exposures are not settled, and the Company keeps its tax liabilities after Completion.

---

**Priority for next turn:** N-008 (Bluefen), N-009 (Riverlark), N-005 (fraud), N-006 (disclosure) and N-004 (title). These either block Completion or remove core protection. Before the mark-up goes out, confirm with the Wattlebridge deal team whether any principal-level position actually exists.
